Mugabe Tribute: Liberator Turned Dictator

By: Siniketiwe Hlanze | Production

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
One of Africa's longest serving presidents has tonight we reflect on his life and politics.

Unique Selling Point:
After almost 40years in office,disastrous economic policies and violent repression. Robert Mugabe has died.

Summary:
The insert will look at the life of Robert Mugabe and his rule of Zimbabwe over the decades, highlighting his political and economic stance which have had dire effects on his country and people. This is plorising figure as he is celebrated as a Pan Africanist and for his very strong anti-west stance.

Further information:
The piece will primary draw from archive footage.

Script:


Liberator - firebrand and uncompromising in his ideologies the man who led the ZANU-PF on the just cause for Zimbabwe’s independence from British colonial rule in 1980. Robert Gabriel Mugabe served first as prime minister then later as president. became Zimbabwe’s second president (find year), entrusted with leading what was one of Africa’s self-sufficient countries – with an ample agricultural yield, abundant in minerals and a nation of astute citizens. Shortly after independence –the Zimbabwean National Army unleashed unspeakable violence on dissidents in parts of the Matabeleland and Midlands regions.

The Gukurahundi mass murders were carried out by a North-Korean trained unit 5th brigade – claiming 20 000 lives, mainly Ndebele speaking people. Mugabe’s iron fist would signify the next 37 years in office. He used the army to crackdown on his critics – brutal violence and persecution were used to stifle opposition. The crackdown would intensify during election periods –and opposition leaders such as Morgan Tsvwangarai of the Movement for Democratic Change – were targets of torture and endless detention. For President Robert Mugabe, his reign was ordained by a higher power – In 2008 he claimed that “not the opposition – but only God would remove him.” As his people haemorrhaged under international sanctions, fuel pumps ran dry and food became too expensive – but President Robert Mugabe remained resolute in his policies and stance that he would not step down It was the radical land reform policy and indigenization that propelled Zimbabwe’s economic decline.

With an almost collapsed economy and political repression – Many Zimbabweans left the country. The man once celebrated as the country’s founding father– was now berated at home and abroad. President Robert Mugabe - One of Africa’s longest serving statesmen - would go down in history as one of the continent’s dictators A former teacher, an eloquent speaker, described by those close to him as charming, a man with a penchant for smart suits. He enjoyed a life of comfort and luxury. In his ailing years Robert Mugabe would regularly travel to Asia for medical attention, leaving behind a broken health system in his country.

In 2017– following mounting pressure from thousands of Zimbabweans, the army and quarters within the ruling the ZANU PF. Mugabe resigned Then 93 years old it was a betrayal which pushed him to turn his back on the party he founded. He told the world that his ousting was a coup Mugabe spent the last two years away from the public eye – as the country he ruled since 1980 – has tried to build new life without him The figure admired not only fighting for his country’s liberation but advocating for the independence many other African countries and his anti-West stance. In the wake of his passing President Emmerson Mnangagwa has said Robert Mugabe will be remembered as a national hero But For Zimbabweans at home and abroad – Robert Gabriel Mugabe’s hero status will remain a contentious issue legacy remains a contested issue? – died in hospital in Singapore where he had been receiving round the clock medical attention - many miles from the broken down and destitute healthcare system in Zimbabwe
